physical: A spring pushes back in proportion to how far it is stretched; stretching it further takes more force, more so the stiffer the spring. F = k × x
reflected_sentence: The further the reach into Vibration, the more Frequency it asks; but where the spring's stiffness set the price, receptivity now eases it, and the ask falls as receptivity rises.
rule_reason: One listed cost: stretching further gets harder and rises with the spring constant, which carries resistance as stiffness; one odd cost turns the reading around.
interpretation: Frequency is asked in proportion to Vibration, and the proportion that was stiffness now reads as receptivity. The product keeps its shape; the condition flips. What got harder with a stiffer spring gets easier with a more receptive one.
closing: Shape was rule-decided: one cost, rising with the spring constant, which the resistance list defines as opposition to deformation, so the odd count turns it. The one judgment-adjacent move was lexical: spring constant has no frozen partner, and I used receptivity, the legal word for the flipped condition, in the reflected formula rather than inventing a word; this is flagged in unmapped_terms so the substitution is on record.
